objective: Convert large numbers to and from scientific notation
hints: Read the requested direction and the exponent instead of assuming a fixed number of places.

To write scientific notation, move the decimal until the coefficient is at least one and less than ten, then record the number of places as a positive exponent; to write an ordinary number, expand the positive power of ten.
Check that the scientific and ordinary representations have exactly the same place value.

constraints: negative exponent for numbers less than 1
hints: Read the requested direction and the negative exponent.

To form scientific notation, move the small decimal right until its coefficient is at least one and strictly less than ten; the number of rightward places becomes the magnitude of the negative exponent. To form an ordinary decimal, shift according to the given negative exponent and preserve leading zeros.
Check that both forms represent exactly the same small positive value.

constraints: renormalize the coefficient into [1, 10); compare exponents before coefficients
hints: Normalize each supplied scientific expression first, shifting its decimal and compensating its exponent so the value stays unchanged.
For a notation task, stop when the coefficient is at least one and less than ten; for a comparison, compare normalized exponents first and coefficients only when the exponents match.
Give the requested normalized form or comparison result for the original expressions.
Multiply the numerical coefficients separately.
Add the exponents of ten, because equal-base powers are being multiplied.
Normalize the result: shift any out-of-range coefficient until it is at least one and strictly less than ten, and compensate the exponent.
Divide the numerical coefficients and subtract the denominator exponent of ten from the numerator exponent.
If the coefficient is below one, move its decimal right and decrease the exponent by the same number of places; if it is at least ten, move left and increase the exponent.
Write the exact normalized coefficient times ten to the resulting integer exponent.
Perform the stated coefficient product or quotient and combine the powers of ten with the matching exponent rule.
Normalize an oversized coefficient by shifting left and increasing the exponent; normalize a positive coefficient below one by shifting right and decreasing the exponent.
Verify that the normalized coefficient is at least one and less than ten and that the decimal shift preserved the value.

constraints: matching exponents; add or subtract coefficients only
hints: Keep the shared power of ten outside the coefficient calculation.
Add or subtract only the coefficients.
Retain the common power of ten.

constraints: rewrite the smaller-exponent term to match the larger exponent
hints: Rewrite the term with the smaller exponent to use the larger exponent, scaling that term’s coefficient downward by the matching power of ten to preserve value.
Perform the stated addition or subtraction on the aligned coefficients and keep the common power of ten.
Normalize the result until its coefficient is at least one and strictly less than ten, then verify its value against the original expression.
Align the powers of ten when necessary, then perform the stated addition or subtraction on the coefficients.
If the positive coefficient is at least ten, shift left and increase the exponent; if it is below one, shift right and decrease the exponent.
Write the normalized result and check that the coefficient is at least one and strictly less than ten without changing the value.
Interpret a square as the product of two equal copies of the given number.
Multiply those equal factors to find the square.
Use square units only for an area; preserve counting units for an array and use no unit for a pure numerical expression.

objective: Roots of perfect squares up to 144
hints: Identify the radicand and seek its principal, nonnegative square root.
Choose a candidate whose square equals the radicand.
Square the candidate to verify it, and attach a length unit only when the problem supplies an area context.

objective: Larger perfect squares and multiples of ten
hints: Identify the radicand and a candidate principal, nonnegative root.
Check the candidate by ordinary multiplication of the number by itself.
Report the verified root, preserving only units actually supplied by the context.
Evaluate each principal square root before combining terms.
Identify the remaining operation or contextual quantity after the roots are known.
Apply the requested addition, subtraction, or multiplication and preserve any relevant units.

constraints: root of a fraction = root of top over root of bottom
hints: Take the principal roots of the numerator and positive denominator separately.
Form the nonnegative fraction from those roots and simplify it exactly.
Square the fraction to verify that it returns the original radicand.
Evaluate the known principal square roots first.
If a product is requested, multiply the roots; if one factor is missing, divide the known product by the known nonzero factor.
Substitute the result into the original product to verify it.

objective: Bracket a root between consecutive integers
hints: Find consecutive perfect squares surrounding the radicand.
Their roots give consecutive integer bounds.
Choose the requested lower bound.

objective: Round a root to the nearest integer
constraints: compare distances to the two nearest perfect squares
hints: Bracket the radicand between squares of consecutive nonnegative integers.
Square the midpoint between those two integers and compare the radicand with that exact threshold.
Choose the lower integer below the squared-midpoint threshold and the upper integer above it, following the stated tie rule if equality occurs.
For nonnegative competing values, compare them by comparing their squares with each radicand.
Place each root relative to the ordinary numbers, or identify the requested extreme.
Return every original expression in the requested order when an ordering is asked, and return only the requested value for a selection task.
Recall perfect cubes near the radicand.
Find a candidate whose product of three equal factors equals the radicand.
Cube the candidate to verify the real cube root.
A negative cube has a negative cube root.
Find the positive magnitude first.
Attach the negative sign and cube-check it.
Read the actual root index, including whether it is four or five.
Test a small candidate by raising it to that index, using that many equal factors.
Choose the nonnegative principal root for an even index and preserve the real sign for an odd index.

constraints: pull out the largest perfect-square factor
hints: Find the largest perfect-square factor of the radicand, or keep extracting square factors until the remainder is squarefree.
Take the square root of that perfect-square factor outside the radical.
Multiply the extracted factors and leave only a squarefree factor inside the radical.

constraints: multiply any outside coefficient after simplifying
hints: Simplify the radical before multiplying by its outside coefficient.
Extract the largest square factor.
Multiply the outside factors and retain the remaining radical.
Prime-factor the radicand.
Pair identical prime factors; each pair contributes one outside factor.
Multiply the outside factors and leave unpaired primes inside.
